tagline: how the KV cache stopped being a contiguous reservation
source: Mechanism and figures as published in the paper. Nothing on this page was measured here.

panels.title: The KV cache, before it was paged
panels.sub: a request reserves room for the longest answer it might give, and then does not give it
panels.note: in the paper's measurements, 20.4%–38.2% of KV cache memory held actual token state
panels.bottom: paged: fixed-size blocks, allocated when a token needs one
panels.tail: waste is confined to the last block of each sequence
panels.scale: slots, illustrative — vLLM's default block is 16 tokens

panels.title: Contiguous in the table, scattered in memory
panels.sub: the attention kernel is taught to gather its blocks, so they no longer have to be neighbours
panels.note: the block table is the whole trick: virtual memory, for the KV cache
panels.free_note: every other block stays free for someone else

panels.title: One prompt, four answers, one copy of the prompt
panels.sub: blocks are reference-counted, so branches of the same request read the same physical blocks
panels.note: as published: 6.1%–9.8% less KV memory on parallel sampling, 37.6%–55.2% on beam search
panels.cow: a branch that writes gets its own copy of that one block — copy on write
panels.tail: and the paper's headline: 2–4x the throughput at the same latency
panels.prompt_label: one physical copy of the prompt's blocks

panels.title: What paging came to
panels.sub: the memory that stopped being wasted became sequences that could be in flight at the same time
panels.note: more memory held means more sequences batched together, and that is where the throughput comes from

meters.label: KV cache memory holding actual token state
meters.note: vLLM confines waste to the last block of a sequence - under 4%, as published

numbers.caption: throughput at the same latency, against FasterTransformer and Orca
of KV cache memory wasted, against 60-80% in the systems it was compared to
